beats.narration_text: International students looking for data jobs have a short clock, and only some employers sponsor visas. So we apply to sponsors. But many of them have no entry-level data job open today, and those applications go nowhere.

shot.visual_intent: A clock face (a short clock); three sponsor crates; a stack of applications with an arrow to them; grey lamps above the crates (nothing open today); a cross on the arrow (go nowhere).

beats.narration_text: SponsorScout tells the student, for each sponsor, whether to apply, network, check by hand, or skip, with the public record behind every answer. A strong sponsor with nothing open isn't dropped. It goes on a networking list.

beats.answers: limits + why it matters to me
beats.narration_text: It never applies, emails, or contacts anyone. The person decides. I'm building it because I'm job hunting too, and I wanted a smarter strategy than a hundred-plus applications a day.

shot.visual_intent: Application, email and message icons slide to a dark wall and are crossed out; a list 'you decide'. Then a pile of applications ('100+ a day') gives way to one short list.

beats.narration_text: What already exists? My Visa Jobs lists sponsors and their past job counts; I looked at it in October. H one B Grader grades employers on past approvals and denials. Interstride, which universities provide, shows sponsorship history and filters jobs by visa.

shot.visual_intent: Three plain panels, names in text only: MyVisaJobs (rows of past-count bars), H1BGrader (a letter grade), Interstride (a history bar row and filter chips).
shot.motion_claim: Three plain panels, names in text only: MyVisaJobs (rows of past-count bars), H1BGrader (a letter grade), Interstride (a history bar row and filter chips).

beats.narration_text: The Reallocation Engine's own scorer, which I had Claude Code run in October, gives a sponsor with no open job a zero, and skips it. These tools show who sponsored before, or what's open now. None that I found turns a proven sponsor with nothing open into a networking target. That's the gap.

shot.visual_intent: A sponsor crate with a dark lamp. Top path, grey and dashed: engine scorer -> 0 -> skip. Bottom path, solid: SponsorScout -> network list; the crate travels into it; 'the gap' lands beside it.
shot.motion_claim: A sponsor crate with a dark lamp. Top path, grey and dashed: engine scorer -> 0 -> skip. Bottom path, solid: SponsorScout -> network list; the crate travels into it; 'the gap' lands beside it.

beats.narration_text: The data is public. Sponsorship records from the Eighty Days to Stay file. Recent funding from S E C Form D filings. Open jobs from the public Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby job boards. The job seeker is fictional.

beats.narration_text: Each sponsor gets three checks: has it sponsored data roles, has it raised money recently, and is an entry-level data job open today? The answers set the verdict. The prototype ran on October third, on one hundred twenty-three sponsors.

shot.visual_intent: A moving conveyor through three depth-correct gates; each lamp pulses on its question; '123 sponsors · Oct 3'.
shot.motion_claim: A moving conveyor through three depth-correct gates; each lamp pulses on its question; '123 sponsors · Oct 3'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: But only sixteen of them had a known job board, so most answers were check by hand. So, with Claude Code, I built a board resolver. It tries names built from each company's name, one request at a time, saves every raw response with a fingerprint, and stops when it's done, out of budget, or hitting errors.

shot.visual_intent: '16 / 123 known boards'; the resolver block; a three-step loop (try a name -> one request -> save + fingerprint) with a return arrow; a stop panel: done · budget · errors.
shot.motion_claim: '16 / 123 known boards'; the resolver block; a three-step loop (try a name -> one request -> save + fingerprint) with a return arrow; a stop panel: done · budget · errors.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It only proposes. I approve or refuse each board, and my decision is tied to the fingerprint of the response I saw. It can only read from those three sites, and it has no way to send anything.

shot.visual_intent: A proposal sheet with a real fingerprint (c50b5646d54e, Anaplan) -> a dark gate square 'my decision' -> approve / refuse trays; 'reads 3 sites only · no way to send'.
shot.motion_claim: A proposal sheet with a real fingerprint (c50b5646d54e, Anaplan) -> a dark gate square 'my decision' -> approve / refuse trays; 'reads 3 sites only · no way to send'.

beats.narration_text: How will I know it worked? First, coverage. On November twenty-third, the resolver made six hundred twenty-nine requests, all to the three allowed sites, and found candidate boards for thirty-nine companies. After my review, coverage went from sixteen to fifty, of one hundred twenty-three.

shot.visual_intent: '629 requests · 3 sites only'; '39 candidates'; the coverage bar fills from 16/123 to 50/123 (real, after G1); the number changes 16 -> 50.
shot.motion_claim: '629 requests · 3 sites only'; '39 candidates'; the coverage bar fills from 16/123 to 50/123 (real, after G1); the number changes 16 -> 50.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It also got things wrong, in ways I could check. Five boards belonged to other companies, like a childcare center. Claude flagged them, and I refused all five. The name check called Weight Watchers a mismatch, though it's the right company. Five approved boards are empty, and sixty-seven companies showed no board under the names it tried.

shot.visual_intent: Two board sheets with their real names (Slice Talent Community; The Village Learning Center), crossed; '5 refused'. Then: 'Weight Watchers' marked mismatch but right; an empty tray '5 empty'; '67 no board found'.
shot.motion_claim: Two board sheets with their real names (Slice Talent Community; The Village Learning Center), crossed; '5 refused'. Then: 'Weight Watchers' marked mismatch but right; an empty tray '5 empty'; '67 no board found'.

beats.answers: how the verdicts will be judged
beats.narration_text: Next, the verdicts. Before tuning anything, I'll set aside a hand-checked set of sponsors. If fewer than nine in ten apply verdicts are right on that set, it didn't work. And after fourteen days, I'll re-check the networking targets for new postings. This sample can show what it gets wrong. It can't show that anyone gets hired.

shot.visual_intent: A sealed dashed box 'held-out set · set aside first'; a bar with a threshold tick at 9/10 'apply verdicts right'; a 14-day grid; 'can show: what it gets wrong' / 'can't show: hires'.
shot.motion_claim: A sealed dashed box 'held-out set · set aside first'; a bar with a threshold tick at 9/10 'apply verdicts right'; a 14-day grid; 'can show: what it gets wrong' / 'can't show: hires'.
